rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal structure present anywhere in this lecture.
Chunk 0 is a standard title/lede slide; chunks 1-5 each carry 2-4 self-carrying bullets/paragraphs, none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Each header matches its chunk's content: 'Eval' names the term the chunk defines; 'One primitive, placed wherever there's a bar' matches the reuse-across-contexts content; 'The eval primitive scales unchanged' matches the Intercom-at-scale content; 'The primitive that runs on cadence' matches the scheduling-primitives content; 'Why the loop survives the model' matches the model-churn/stance content. None contradicted by its own chunk.

No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere. Two parallel-structure passages checked against the anaphora/epistrophe rule and cleared because every leg carries new concrete content, not an empty/generic third leg: chunk 1's 'Judge when... Verifier when... Gate when...' (three distinct check-mechanisms: LLM-read / deterministic / CI-placement) and chunk 5's fresh-edited 'Reference because the goal drifts. Plan because the window fills. Verifier because plausible-but-wrong is the default failure mode of a statistical machine. Encode because a lesson learned once and not written down gets learned again next week.' (four distinct concrete reasons, no repetition). Chunk 2's 'On a pull request. On a nightly run. On the next agent... On the team's shared kit.' likewise four concrete, distinct placements. No self-grading superlative. No number+own-retraction (Intercom numbers in chunk 3 are stated plainly, no hedge-then-undercut). No abstraction-noun stacks (bounded-window-reality style) — 'kit', 'primitive', 'stance' are concrete/ordinary, not stacked abstractions. No empty-leg verb triplet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.

Not scored as dialect. 'kit', 'primitive', 'stance', 'shape' are AE101 taught/spine vocabulary or ordinary engineering words, not maintainer dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture headings read as claims/definitional labels, not imperatives or exercise-style phase labels: 'One primitive, placed wherever there's a bar', 'The eval primitive scales unchanged', 'The primitive that runs on cadence', 'Why the loop survives the model' are all declarative. 'Eval' (chunk 1) is a single-word header but functions as the naming beat's own claim (this section's job is asserting 'this is called eval') rather than a task instruction or phase label — no imperative-vs-declarative mood confusion results, the harm this rule guards against.
